newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 20.

text.p: The following were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) Chairman Arjun Deraniyagala announces 150 billion rupee master plan to provide electricity to meet demand beyond year 2015.
A Colombo magistrate orders resident in fashionable Colombo residential area to pay CEB nearly quarter of a million rupees for power piracy.

Main opposition United National Party (UNP) appeals to government to stop violence against its members after police held some of them responsible for last week's killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker.
Government decides to limit issue of firearms to members of parliament and local politicians after last week's killing of ruling coalition lawmaker.

Member of parliament Dilan Perera testifying at inquiry into the killing of ruling coalition lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala says he saw UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame shooting at Ellawala. Punchinilame is still at large.

Colomb magistrate upholds petition by lawyers of one of the main suspects in last week's killing, Mahinda Ratnatilleke, to keep suspect from being taken to Ratnapura for inquiry, given present tense conditions there.
Government troops kill seven Tamil Tiger rebels at Nadunkerni in estern Welioya region.
